messages.subject: Re: Starglyph plot
parts:
Hello- I am trying to create a starglyph plot in polar coordinates, with months radiating as spokes:

My data:

month.abbr <- c(“Jan", “Feb", “Mar", “Apr”, “May", “Jun", “Jul", “Aug", “Sep", “Oct", “Nov", “Dec”)

avg.hours <- 4.5

state.hours <- c(2.94, 3.02, 4.98, 5.03, 5.08, 5.76, 5.13, 4.63, 5.00, 4.45, 2.45, 2.03)

df <- data.frame(month.abbr, avg.hours, state.hours)

A feeble plotting attempt:

ggplot(data = df, aes(x = month.abbr, y = state.hours, group=1)) + geom_line() + coord_polar()

issues I would like to correct:
- the states are in seemingly random order
- Jan should be at 12 o’clock
- the graph should be a closed loop
- I would like to add a ring of df$avg.hours (ie, a second plot)

Thank you in advance for any help.

PS- incidentally, following Winston Chang’s site to generate the above, it is unclear to me why i’m not calling ‘qplot’ instead of ‘ggplot’.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Starglyph plot
parts:
Hi:

(i) I changed the name of the data frame since df() is a built-in R function.
(ii) There is an object named month.abb that already does the
three-character month abbreviation, and you can use it to generate a
factor with consecutive months as labels. This takes care of the month
ordering problem.
(iii) The data frame is constructed so that all of the necessary data
is in the data frame rather than in both the data frame and the global
workspace.

avg.hours <- 4.5
DF <- data.frame(Month = factor(month.abb, levels = month.abb),
state.hours = c(2.94, 3.02, 4.98, 5.03, 5.08, 5.76,
5.13, 4.63, 5.00, 4.45, 2.45, 2.03))

library(ggplot2)

Here are a couple of options:

1. Star plot version:
# Star plot
ggplot(data = df, aes(x = month.abbr, y = state.hours, group = 1)) +

geom_line() + coord_polar(theta = "x", start = -pi/12) + ylim(0, 6)

The visual drawback is that there is no connection between the
December and January values, and it is not at all obvious that there
should be. One way to mitigate the problem a bit is to use
geom_ribbon():

ggplot(data = DF, aes(x = Month, y = state.hours, group = 1)) +
geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = state.hours), fill = "darkorange",
alpha = 0.3) +
geom_line() +
geom_abline(intercept = avg.hours, slope = 0, size = 1, color = "blue") +
coord_polar(theta = "x", start = -pi/12)


A more aesthetically pleasing display that conveys the same
information is the coxcomb plot.

2. Coxcomb plot version

ggplot(data = DF, aes(x = Month, y = state.hours, group = 1)) +
geom_bar(width = 1, stat = "identity", fill = "darkorange",
color = "black") +
geom_abline(intercept = avg.hours, slope = 0,
size = 1, color = "blue") +
coord_polar(theta = "x", start = -pi/12)


The value of start moves the position of the January grid line to the
top (-15 degrees, or -pi/12 radians). In the star plot, I inserted a
ylim() command so that the center of the display corresponded to y =
0. This is unnecessary in the coxcomb plot because the bar geometry
automatically sets the bottom at y = 0.

Re your last question, there's no reason why you couldn't start with
qplot(); some people just prefer one over the other. I'm in Winston's
camp :)

Dennis
